subject: Rebaseline: AcmeFin POC scope & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmefin.com>; Jane Smith <jane.smith@acmefin.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + POC plan (AcmeFin)

Thanks again for your time today, John and Jane — good conversation. Below is a short recap and the proposed POC plan we discussed. Please confirm or highlight anything we missed.

Recap from discovery call:
- Primary objective: validate Redwood inference for risk-scoring and transaction classification latency/cost at 95th percentile.
- Key datasets: anonymized transactions (50k rows) + historical labels for fraud/risk classification.
- Stakeholders: John Doe (Head of ML), Jane Smith (PM, Risk Ops), Rishi Malhotra (AM, Redwood)

Proposed POC plan (initial baseline):
- Duration: 3 weeks (kickoff next week)
- Success criteria (must-haves):
  1) End-to-end latency for 95th percentile inference under realistic load <= 450ms per request
  2) Precision/recall for high-risk class within 5% of their current production model on blind holdout set
  3) Cost target: <= $0.015 per inference (token-normalized metric — we'll provide breakdown)
- Deliverables: weekly demo + final evaluation report, SOW attached (poc-sow-v1.pdf)
- Ownership: Redwood SE (Dev) for integration + Redwood AM (Rishi) for commercial items; Acme to provide anonymized dataset and a dedicated test endpoint

Next steps:
1) John/Jane: confirm acceptance of success criteria and kickoff window by EOD Monday
2) Acme: share sample dataset (S3 link or secure upload) and allow test account creation
3) Redwood: schedule kickoff + allocate SE time

Thanks — I'll follow up early next week with a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Attachment: poc-sow-v1.pdf (SOW draft, 3 pages)

From: John Doe <john.doe@acmefin.com>

Cc: Jane Smith <jane.smith@acmefin.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + POC plan (AcmeFin)

Thanks Marissa — this is a great summary. A couple of asks from our side after internal sync: 

1) We want to add a second use case to the POC mid-trial — transaction classification for chargeback detection. It's higher priority for Ops and will help justify the integration. Can we include it as part of the evaluation?
2) If we add that use case, we need to rebaseline success criteria (specifically precision/recall targets) and adjust timelines.
3) Jane will coordinate dataset delivery, but we likely need an additional labeled holdout (10k items) specifically for the chargeback flow.

Assuming Redwood agrees to include this, can you propose an updated timeline and indicate any additional SE time or cost impact?

Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap + POC plan (AcmeFin) — request to add chargeback use case

Quick internal note — technically feasible with caveats: 

- We can run two classification flows in the same POC, but adding the chargeback use case will push the effective delivery by ~1 week to account for data ingestion, label validation, and an extra evaluation pass. So proposed POC duration becomes 4 weeks.
- SE effort estimate: 20–30 hours (integration + evaluation + extra tuning).
- Data format: CSV or parquet with the following minimal cols: transaction_id, amount, timestamp, merchant_id, label_chargeback (0/1). Prefer parquet for throughput.
- Model/config: start with the same model family we planned; if precision is below target after tuning, we recommend enabling a larger variant (quantization still supported) — potential cost delta we can quantify after the first eval pass.

I updated a short note with the rebaseline bullets and timeline (attached: poc-rebaseline-notes.docx). No SOW update required for the scope shift itself for this POC stage; if Acme asks for a guaranteed SLA or longer-run dedicated capacity, we'll need a new SOW.

Happy to hop on a quick call with the Acme team if they want to walk through the tradeoffs.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + POC plan (AcmeFin) — updated plan and timeline

Hi John/Jane — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal confirmation from Dev, we can include chargeback classification as an additional use case with the following changes: 

Rebaseline summary:
- New duration: 4 weeks (kickoff as originally proposed)
- New success criteria:
  • Latency: 95th <= 550ms for combined endpoints under target load (we’re increasing threshold slightly to allow room for two pipelines)
  • Classification quality: precision/recall for both risk and chargeback classes within 7% of your production baselines on the respective holdouts
  • Cost target: revised to <= $0.018 per inference (token-normalized); detailed breakdown in final report
- SE effort: ~25 hours (integration + evaluation + one tuning cycle) — included in POC; no additional commercial charge for this change at the POC stage
- Data request: Acme to provide additional labeled holdout of ~10k rows for chargeback cases; preferred parquet format, S3 URL or secure upload
- Deliverables: weekly check-ins, mid-POC demo (end of week 2), final report (end of week 4)

If that works, can you confirm dataset delivery timeline and acceptance of the rebaseline? Once we have your confirmation I will update the internal kickoff invite and share the revised evaluation plan (link to drive doc included).

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
